name: Hopia

project_scope.note: Current genus for source-pool Panicum obtusum.

fast_fill_note: Canonical PASS Hopia obtusa now has a 3-image FAST-FILL gallery. One field image is filed under the settled synonym Panicum obtusum; reproductive closeups use exact-species iNaturalist photo records.
look_here_first: VINE MESQUITE Hopia obtusa: seek an actually connected stolon to hairy SWOLLEN ROOTING node; next its slender inflorescence of BLUNT oval spikelets. Older source name Panicum obtusum is the same accepted species, NOT generic Panicum.

recognition.where_to_look_first: VINE MESQUITE: FIRST trace a long creeping aboveground STOLON away from a leafy shoot; examine a swollen, densely hairy node where a new plant can root. THEN look at the narrow upright seedhead: short appressed raceme-like branches carry conspicuous smooth, rounded/oval blunt spikelets (not bermudagrass's radiating fingers). A tiny membranous ligule at the blade/sheath junction confirms a grass collar character but is not identified from the current photographs. Spikelets and root-bearing nodes must belong to the same plant.
priority: Follow a connected aboveground runner to a hairy swollen root-forming node
Find the slender upright inflorescence; separate short appressed branches from Cynodon's terminal fingers
Check actual smooth blunt oval ~3–4 mm attached spikelets with scale
Confirm true inner membranous ligule under a lens, not fuzzy node hairs
recognition.field_caution: Vine mesquite can grow alongside turf grasses; ensure runner and flower belong to same rooted individual.

comparison_lesson.title: Hopia vs bermudagrass, switchgrass and buffalograss
comparison_lesson.memory_rule: RUNNER + HAIRY SWOLLEN ROOTING NODE + NARROW, BLUNT OVAL-SPIKELET HEAD = vine mesquite candidate. Bermudagrass's terminal fingers are different. Confirm an intact plant.
quick_split: BERMUDAGRASS (Cynodon dactylon) also creeps by stolons but usually has 3–7 slender DIGITATE one-sided fingers radiating near one point, rather than Hopia's narrow head of short appressed branches with stout blunt OVAL spikelets; its ligule is a short hair-fringed membranous rim. SWITCHGRASS (Panicum virgatum) normally forms taller erect clumps from rhizomes with a large open much-branched panicle, not vine mesquite's long aboveground node-rooting stolons. BUFFALOGRASS (Bouteloua dactyloides) is low sod-forming and dioecious, with contrasting separate male/female flowering structures rather than vine mesquite's oval spikelets. Do not identify from a vegetative patch or seedhead shape alone; trace the node and examine attached spikelets.
comparison_lesson.guardrail: Current genus has only Hopia obtusa installed. Panicum obtusum is its synonym, not an extra species. Keep original county/native PASS and image rights unchanged.

comparison_matrix.title: One-genus-member Hopia field key
rows: Cynodon has radiating thin terminal fingers; Hopia has short appressed inflorescence branches and plump blunt oval spikelets
Large airy switchgrass panicle and upright rhizomatous habit vs Hopia's long swollen-node rooting stolons
Low buffalograss bears quite different male and female inflorescences; no Hopia-like clustered round spikelets

what_to_teach_crew: Follow one runner from old shoot to new shoot; distinguish aboveground stolon from detached dry leaves.
Inspect one visibly hairy swollen node and ask whether it is actually rooting.
At the seedhead, find short appressed branches bearing smooth blunt oval spikelets; do not confuse multiple branches with bermudagrass's fingers.
Find the membranous inner ligule; hair on a stolon node is a DIFFERENT structure.
Apply synonym Panicum obtusum when older books label vine mesquite, but keep Hopia obtusa as canonical.
visual_needs: Same rooted Hopia plant photographed wide enough to trace one long aboveground stolon to a new rooted shoot; include a metric scale.
10–20× macro of an ACTUAL swollen hairy stolon node visibly emitting adventitious roots; do not arrow a nonrooting joint.
1-mm-scale inner MEMBRANOUS ligule at the leaf blade/sheath junction, with collar hairs separately visible if present.
10–20× side and face views of an intact attached ~3–4 mm rounded blunt spikelet showing glumes/veins; avoid claiming venation from distant seedheads.
Matched same-scale comparison: Hopia appressed branches and oval spikelets versus Cynodon digitately arranged thin one-sided fingers.

items.label: 3 · INFLORESCENCE — narrow rows of blunt spikelets
items.image_role: Existing exact-species iNaturalist macro source, visible short narrow inflorescence branchlets and oval spikelets held in a hand
items.caption: Several slender portions of vine mesquite's seedhead are held over fingers for scale. Along them are closely spaced, plump, blunt OVAL spikelets. This photo does not show the runner, rooting node, or membrane ligule; count no imaginary awns or reproductive micro-organs.
items.why_it_matters: Bermudagrass carries narrow one-sided spikelet-bearing fingers radiating from a common point; Hopia has a slender, compact-looking head with short closely appressed branches and rounded larger spikelets.
